newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Investors should watch Taiwan stock basics -Chiu.
newsitem.headline: Investors should watch Taiwan stock basics -Chiu.

text.p: Taiwan Finance Minister Paul Chiu urged investors on Thursday to watch the fundamentals when investing in the rallying stock market, but declined to say whether share prices were overvalued.
"It's up to investors to determine whether it's healthy for the index to stand above 10,000," Chiu told reporters after the index closed in five digits for the first time since 1990.
"Investors should pay attention to stocks' fundamentals. They should evaluate the risks and take full responsibility for their decisions," Chiu said.

The share index, which tested above 10,000 on Tuesday but failed to hold its gains, soared comfortably past the threshold on Thursday to close at a seven-year peak of 10,066.35, a gain of 123.56 points or 1.24 percent. It was the highest close since the index finished at 10,907.09 on April 4, 1990.

Chiu's comment was conspicuously more cautious than those of Premier Lien Chan and Liu Tai-ying, a ruling Nationalist Party leader who controls the party's US$3.1 billion in assets, who have said it was "healthy" for the index to surpass 10,000.
Analysts have said the comments by Lien and Liu had helped the index breach psychological resistance at 10,000.
A straw poll conducted after Thursday's market close by Reuters Financial Television forecast that Taiwan's benchmark stock index would rise to 10,792 at the end of 1997.
Brokers at six institutions were unanimous that the index would surpass its all-time high close of 12,495 sometime in the third quarter but faced uncertainty in the fourth.
